title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams
content:
Releasing your first album is a big step for any artist, but for Jazzy it's one that's followed some huge strides.
The Irish singer and DJ has been streamed more than a billion times and worked with industry heavyweights including Calvin Harris.
If that's not enough, on Saturday she has her biggest gig yet when she'll be playing tracks like No Bad Vibes and Someday in front of a home crowd in Dublin.
For Jazzy, writing an album has always been in the back of her mind and now, finally, it's time to hit send.
She's previously released dozens of singles, building up a monthly listenership over 10 million strong, but Peace and Patience is her first full-length work.
"It's been quite a few years of creating some smaller projects," she tells BBC Newsbeat.
"That's given me enough experience now to feel like it was the right moment."
The 30-year-old, real name Yasmine Byrne, has been putting out music for more than five years and collabed with the likes of Sonny Fodera, Rossi. and KILIMANJARO on some of her biggest tracks.
Dance music has boomed in recent years, with Spotify previously telling Newsbeat that since 2020 the amount under-25s listen to the genre has grown by more than 73% globally.
It also dominated festival line-ups over the summer - including Radio 1's Big Weekend which dedicated all its stages to dance music on the opening night.
But artists in the genre have often moved away from albums, opting instead to release EPs and singles.
Jazzy has noticed the change, saying it feels "a lot different now, with people kind of siding with virality rather than quality of music".
"When I was making the album, I wasn't thinking about going viral or anything like that. I just wanted to make something that was true to me and sounded like a Jazzy album.
"I like to let things happen quite organically and I try to just let the music speak to me."
Jazzy is rooted in the Dublin club scene, starting her career as part of a group called Powerful Creative Minds in the city.
But as more and more clubs close, the DJ says there are fewer opportunities for artists to cut their teeth offline.
"When I first started going out, there was a lot more going on," she says.
"There was a lot more nightclubs to go to and it's very different when we look at it now, which is sad.
"There's definitely a home for dance music on the internet of course but club culture is very important and I think that's something that we need to keep going for sure."
Latest figures from the Night Time Industries Association suggest about 12 venues are closing across the UK every month, with almost 30% of the night time economy lost since the coronavirus pandemic.

final_quality.reason: The article reports a significant development in the music industry, specifically in the dance music genre, with Jazzy's debut album release after achieving over a billion streams. The article provides context about the growth of dance music popularity and Jazzy's own experiences as an artist, making it a relevant and newsworthy story for entertainment enthusiasts.

title: Final James Bond screen tests to take place this weekend, reports say
content:
Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor are among the actors thought to be taking part in final auditions to play James Bond, according to reports.
Screen tests are said to be taking place this weekend, possibly as early as Friday, according to the Hollywood Reporter , with between three and five actors understood to have reached the last stages of the process.
The finalists are said to be taking part in auditions with three components - stunts, camera presence and dialogue.
Deadline reported the screen tests had been due take place in early October, but had been delayed by scheduling conflicts, while Variety said Turner and Lowden "appear to be in the mix" to replace Daniel Craig.
British actors Aaron Taylor-Johnson and James Norton were previously connected to the role, while Irish actor Paul Mescal's name had also been thrown into the mix.
Other actors now appear to be in the frame, but reports on the current casting situation vary.
Variety suggested Slow Horses star Lowden may now be edging ahead, while Masters of the Air star Turner was speculated about earlier this year, with some fans suggesting his wife Dua Lipa could sing the Bond theme song.
Sources told Deadline that at least four final screen test offers have been made, and while unconfirmed, "three of the four expected to test are Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor".
O'Connor is best known for playing Prince Charles in The Crown, and for starring in 2025's Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery, with Craig.
Jack O'Connell had been thought to be in the mix, but sources said this may no longer be the case, while Euphoria and Wuthering Heights Star Jacob Elordi is not thought to be testing.
Other stars who were previously linked with the role include The King's Man star Harris Dickinson, along with SAS: Rogue Heroes' Jack Barton.
Deadline said: "Even with the tests wrapping next week, there is no timeline for when a final decision will be made."
Amazon MGM Studios, who now control the Bond franchise, announced in May that the casting process was under way, but had no further comment at the time.
In August, Amy Pascal, one of the next film's producers, told Deadline the "end of the year is a good bet" for possible news on who would be playing Bond.
"We are being really, really methodical. Having worked with Barbara Broccoli at the studio, I mean, Daniel Craig is a hard act to follow," she said.
"And it's got to be something really different that is a stirring and exciting and different."
The BBC's Lizo Mzimba reported in September that "for a series where the stakes are so high, no expense is spared in ensuring that the film team know exactly how each auditionee will come across on screen".
He added: "As the 007 team themselves have explained in the past: 'Bond screen tests are elaborate affairs involving hair and make-up, costumes, sets, and other actors'."
Only six actors have ever played novelist Ian Fleming's British Secret Service agent 007 in the official film series - Sean Connery, Roger Moore, George Lazenby, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.
The last announcement of a new Bond was in 2005 with Craig, who last starred in the role in 2021's No Time to Die, directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga.

final_quality.reason: The article reports on the final stages of the James Bond casting process, providing a clear reason for readers to care: the potential for a new Bond actor to be announced. The inclusion of various actors' names and the details of the screen test process provide substance and interest for fans of the franchise.
